content: 1. Reduce the dose of eliglustat from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily in patients who are extensive metabolizers. 2. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. 3. Cimetidine also increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, so close monitoring is recommended. 4. Eluxadoline increases cimetidine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Cimetidine increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, exercise caution when co-administering with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors. 7. Enasidenib increases cimetidine levels or effects through mechanisms not fully understood. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Avoid co-administration of enasidenib with sensitive substrates of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP transporters, as even minimal concentration changes can lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. 9. Cimetidine increases encainide levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. 10. Encorafenib increases cimetidine levels or effects through mechanisms not fully understood. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 11. Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicities of BCRP substrates. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and consider dose adjustments for these substrates. 12. Cimetidine increases epirubicin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Cimetidine increases the area under the curve (AUC) of epirubicin by 50%. Discontinue cimetidine during epirubicin treatment and monitor closely. 13. Cimetidine increases eplerenone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Erdafitinib increases cimetidine levels by decreasing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 15. Erdafitinib increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after P-gp substrate administration. 16. Cimetidine increases ergotamine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Cimetidine decreases erlotinib levels or effects through mechanisms not fully understood. Avoid combination when possible. If concurrent use is required, administer erlotinib 10 hours after an H2-antagonist and at least 2 hours before the next H2-antagonist dose. 18. Cimetidine increases erythromycin base levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Cimetidine increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Cimetidine increases erythromycin lactobionate levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Cimetidine increases erythromycin stearate levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Eslicarbazepine acetate increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Cimetidine increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Cimetidine increases conjugated synthetic estrogens levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Cimetidine increases esterified estrogens levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Cimetidine increases estropipate levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Cimetidine increases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Cimetidine increases ethosuximide levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Cimetidine increases etoposide levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Cimetidine increases etravirine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Cimetidine increases etravirine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Etravirine increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is recommended. 33. Cimetidine increases eucalyptus levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Cimetidine increases everolimus levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Cimetidine and famciclovir interactions involve aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition. However, clinical studies show no significant effects on penciclovir formation. 36. Cimetidine increases fedratinib levels or effects through mechanisms not fully understood. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Avoid co-administration of fedratinib, a CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 substrate, with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors. The effects of such co-administration have not been studied. 38. Felbamate increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Cimetidine increases felodipine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Felodipine increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Cimetidine increases fentanyl levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. If co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 43. Cimetidine decreases ferric maltol levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Cimetidine decreases ferrous fumarate levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Cimetidine decreases ferrous gluconate levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cimetidine decreases ferrous sulfate levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Cimetidine increases fesoterodine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Cimetidine increases fesoterodine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 49. Cimetidine increases fezolinetant levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 50. Fezolinetant AUC and peak plasma concentration are increased when co-administered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. 51. Cimetidine increases finerenone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 53. Cimetidine increases flecainide levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Flecainide dosage should be carefully titrated during therapy initiation. Monitor flecainide plasma concentration when cimetidine is co-administered or discontinued. 55. Cimetidine increases flibanserin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Increased flibanserin adverse effects may occur if co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 57. Fluconazole increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 58. Cimetidine increases fludrocortisone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Cimetidine increases fluoxetine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 60. Fluoxetine increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 61. Cimetidine increases fluphenazine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 62. Cimetidine increases flurbiprofen levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 63. Cimetidine increases fluvastatin levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 64. Cimetidine increases fluvastatin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 65. Cimetidine increases fluvoxamine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 66. Fluvoxamine increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 67. Cimetidine decreases fosamprenavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. 68. Cimetidine increases fosamprenavir levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 69. Cimetidine increases fosaprepitant levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 70. Cimetidine increases fosphenytoin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Fostamatinib increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Concomitant use of fostamatinib may increase concentrations of P-gp substrate drugs. Monitor for toxicities of the P-gp substrate drug, which may require dosage reduction when given concurrently with fostamatinib. 73. Fostemsavir increases cimetidine levels or effects through mechanisms not fully understood. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 74. Fostemsavir inhibits BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration or modify the dose of BCRP substrate co-administered with fostemsavir. 75. Cimetidine decreases gefitinib levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Separate gefitinib and H2-antagonist doses by at least 6 hours. 76. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases cimetidine levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 77. Cimetidine increases glipizide levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 78. Cimetidine increases glyburide levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 79. Cimetidine increases green tea levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 80. Green tea may contain caffeine, and CYP1A2 inhibitors may inhibit the hepatic oxidative metabolism of caffeine. 81. Cimetidine increases haloperidol levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 82. Cimetidine increases hydrocodone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
